items.jobTitle: Student Research Assistants - DEM Modelling and Calibration of Granite for Geothermal Applications
items.jobDescription:
The Fraunhofer Research Institution for Energy Infrastructures and Geotechnologies IEG conducts applied research in integrated energy infrastructures, geothermal energy and sector coupling. Our research contributes to the development of innovative technologies and sustainable solutions for the energy transition. 
 Understanding the mechanical behaviour and fracture processes of rocks is essential for the development of Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) . Numerical simulations using the Discrete Element Method (DEM) help investigate rock deformation, fracture initiation and propagation under different geological and stress conditions. 
 In cooperation with Ruhr University Bochum (Institute for Structural Mechanics) , we are looking for two motivated student research assistants to support our research on DEM modelling and calibration of granite. 
 Be part of change 
 Depending on your interests and qualifications, you will contribute to one of the following research topics: 
 Research Topic 1: Generalized DEM Calibration Strategy for Granite 
 Development of granite mesostructure models considering mineral composition and microstructural heterogeneity 
 Performance of numerical uniaxial compression and Brazilian tests 
 Development and calibration of a generalized parameter strategy for microstructure-informed DEM models 
 Validation of model transferability across different granite compositions 
 Research Topic 2: DEM Modelling and Calibration of Granite under Triaxial Compression 
 Development of simplified granite mesostructure models using random fields 
 Performance of numerical triaxial compression tests under different confining pressures 
 Conducting sensitivity analyses and calibrating numerical model parameters 
 Validation of simulation results against independent experimental datasets 
 What you contribute 
 Current enrolment in a Master's degree programme in Civil Engineering, Subsurface Engineering, Computational Engineering, Geosciences or a related field 
 Solid understanding of solid mechanics ; basic knowledge of fracture mechanics is an advantage 
 Programming experience in Python and an interest in numerical modelling and simulation 
 Ideally, initial experience with the Discrete Element Method (DEM) or other particle-based simulation methods 
 Familiarity with Linux, high-performance computing (HPC) or rock mechanics is an advantage 
 Independent, structured and analytical working style, with an interest in scientific research and interdisciplinary collaboration 
 What we offer 
 Active involvement in applied research on rock mechanics and geothermal energy technologies 
 Hands-on experience with DEM simulations, numerical model calibration, sensitivity analysis and optimization 
 Opportunities to develop skills in scientific programming, open-source research software, HPC and scientific visualization 
 Close collaboration with researchers from Fraunhofer IEG and Ruhr University Bochum , including regular scientific guidance and feedback 
 Flexible working hours that can be combined with your studies 
 Opportunity to continue working on the research topic as part of a Master's thesis 
 A collaborative research environment with the opportunity to contribute your own ideas and develop practical research skills 
 We value and promote the diversity of our employees' skills and therefore welcome all applications – regardless of age, gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, ideology, disability, sexual orientation and identity. Severely disabled persons are given preference in the event of equal suitability. Our tasks are diverse and adaptable – for applicants with disabilities, we work together to find solutions that best promote their abilities. Remuneration according to the general works agreement for employing assistant staff. 
 With its focus on developing key technologies that are vital for the future and enabling the commercial utilization of this work by business and industry, Fraunhofer plays a central role in the innovation process. As a pioneer and catalyst for groundbreaking developments and scientific excellence, Fraunhofer helps shape society now and in the future.

items.jobDescription:
Das Institut für Fahrzeugkonzepte (FK) des Deutschen Zentrums für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR) ist international anerkannt für die Entwicklung von zukünftigen Straßen- und Schienenfahrzeugen, die eine klima- und umweltgerechte Mobilität ermöglichen, sowie ökonomisch attraktiv und gleichzeitig nutzerzentriert sind.
Wir erforschen und demonstrieren die dazu notwendigen Schlüsseltechnologien und pflegen enge Kooperationen mit anderen wissenschaftlichen Einrichtungen sowie Industrie und Politik.
 Das erwartet dich 
 Wir suchen dich im Team für die Entwicklung und Validierung eines neuartigen Messgeräts für Non-exhaust Emissionen. Dabei entwickelst Du ein System zur Erfassung mobiler Aufzeichnungen der Reifenabroll- und Straßengeräusche an einem Testfahrzeug sowie zur Durchführung stationärer Geräuschmessungen im städtischen Umfeld. Mithilfe traditioneller Signalverarbeitungs- und maschineller Lernverfahren trägst Du dazu bei, die Quelle der aufgezeichneten Geräusche zu identifizieren und zu klassifizieren. Zu deinen Aufgaben gehören neben der Durchführung einer Literaturrecherche, die Planung und Optimierung des Messaufbaus, die Datenauswertung sowie die Ermittlung geeigneter Messpositionen am Fahrzeug.
 Deine Aufgaben 
 Literaturrecherche zu akustischen Messverfahren und Verarbeitungsansätzen für die mobile und stationäre Anwendung.
 Planung des mobilen Messaufbaus sowie Auswahl geeigneter Messpositionen am Fahrzeug
 Stationäre Schall- und Lärmmessungen im städtischen Umfeld inkl. dB Analyse und Geräuschklassifizierung
 Anwendung klassischer Signalverarbeitung sowie Methoden des maschinellen Lernens
 Auswertung und aufbereitete Präsentation der Ergebnisse
 Das bringst du mit 
 Laufendes Masterstudium im Bereich Informatik, Fahrzeugtechnik, Mechatronik, Elektrotechnik, Maschinenbau oder verwandter Studiengänge.
 Interesse an Akustik, Messtechnik und digitaler Signalverarbeitung.
 Grundkenntnisse in der Programmierung mit Python und der Datenanalyse. 
 Erste Erfahrungen im Umgang mit Machine Learning Frameworks
 Hohe Eigenverantwortung und strukturierte Arbeitsweise.
 Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

items.jobTitle: Student/in (w/m/d) der Luft- und Raumfahrt, Ingenieurwissenschaften o. ä. (Braunschweig)
items.jobDescription:
Das Institut für Flugführung betreibt in interdisziplinären Forscherteams grundlagen- und anwendungsorientierte Forschung zur optimalen Führung von Luftfahrzeugen am Boden und in der Luft. Dazu nutzt es eine integrierte Versuchsinfrastruktur. Ziel ist es, den Luftraum flexibler und effizienter zu nutzen und Flughäfen auf optimalen Durchsatz auszurichten, bei gleichzeitiger Minimierung des Treibstoffverbrauchs und der Umweltbelastung. 
 Das erwartet dich 
 Die Abteilung Pilotenassistenz entwickelt Systeme zur Unterstützung von Pilot/innen bei der Führung von Flugzeugen und Hubschraubern im zivilen und im militärischen Kontext. Hierbei geht es um die Integration von KI-Lösungen und um neue multimodale Human Machine Interfaces (HMI), bei der an der optimierten Kombination von Sprach-/Sprachbefehls- und cursorbezogenen Eingabegeräten, von 3D-Audio-, taktilen und visuellen Rückkopplungssystemen (Head-up und Head-down) bis hin zu einem komplett virtuellen Cockpit geforscht wird. Dazu gehört auch die Validierung in Simulation und auch im Flugversuch mit den DLR-Testflugzeugen. 
 Darüber hinaus werden zukünftige ATM-Konzepte erforscht, die insbesondere die neuen Fähigkeiten in Navigation und Kommunikation einzelner Flugzeuge optimal nutzen (wie beispielsweise bei der Sektorlosen Flugverkehrsführung) oder die umfassende Analyse und Bewertung großer Verkehrsszenarien hinsichtlich Klimawirkung, Effizienz und Fluglärm.  
 Deine Aufgaben 
 Du hast die Möglichkeit, bei uns deine Studien- oder Abschlussarbeit oder ein Praktikum zu absolvieren. 
 Im Rahmen einer Studien- oder Abschlussarbeit hast du die Möglichkeit, dich in Fragestellungen im Bereich der Luftfahrt einzuarbeiten und zu aktuellen Themen beizutragen. Solche Arbeiten können sowohl die Durchführung eigener Laborversuche, die Auswertung komplexer Datensätze aus Simulationskampagnen, als auch die Entwicklung von Prototypen oder Assistenzsystemen umfassen. Die Betreuung von Studien-/Abschlussarbeiten erfolgt in enger Kooperation mit deiner Universität. Das genaue Thema sprechen wir gern mit dir und deiner Betreuungsperson an deiner Universität ab. 
 Im Rahmen eines Praktikums erhältst du Einblick in die aktuelle Luftfahrtforschung und unsere Simulationsumgebungen. Du hast die Möglichkeit, Laborversuche und Simulationskampagnen zu begleiten, anfallende Datensätze auszuwerten oder uns bei der Entwicklung von Prototypen von Assistenzsystemen und Mensch-Maschine-Schnittstellen zu unterstützen. Die Mindestdauer eines Praktikums beträgt sechs Wochen, längere Praktika werden bevorzugt. Im Anschluss an dein Praktikum ist auch eine Studien- oder Abschlussarbeit möglich. 
 Das bringst du mit 
 laufendes Studium der Luft- und Raumfahrt, Ingenieurwissenschaften, Informatik o. ä. 
 Interesse an der Luftfahrtforschung 
 Spaß am experimentellen Arbeiten in interdisziplinären Teams 
 eigenständige Denkweise 
 Kenntnisse in der Softwareentwicklung und Simulation: Erfahrung mit Programmiersprachen wie C/C++, Python, Java oder Javascript, Messaging Protokollen (AMQP/Rest) und Git 
 Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen! 
 Fragen zu dieser Position ( Kennziffer  3667 ) beantwortet dir gerne:  
 Dr. Bernd Korn   
 Tel.: +49 531 295 2540

As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Auterion, you will play a pivotal role in the successful development, integration and deployment of Auterion-powered drone systems. 
 In this role, you will collaborate closely with the production, hardware engineering, and firmware/software teams, as well as operations, ensuring that every platform transitions smoothly from an airframe concept into a fully validated flying robot ready for deployment. You will serve as the primary technical interface for partners, work closely with them to understand their technical requirements, configure and adapt existing solutions, contribute to core software development, and ensure successful implementation. 
 This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with customer collaboration and system-level problem solving, bridging the gap between hardware, firmware, and real-world flight performance. 
 Responsibilities and Duties 
 Operate in a highly hands-on environment with evolving system requirements, rapidly iterating across hardware and software integration challenges.
 Manage software releases and perform firmware flashing and configuration using PX4 or adjacent autopilot ecosystems, including sensor calibration, ESC tuning, and system bring-up.
 Provide deep avionics and airframe expertise, including autopilot tuning, sensor and payload integration, power systems and airworthiness considerations.

 Participate in flight testing activities to validate platform stability, safety, and mission performance, resolving technical issues often directly in the field during customer trials and demonstrations.
 Contribute to technical documentation and continuous improvement of engineering processes.
 Feed customer and market requirements back into product and engineering teams to influence the roadmap of the Auterion stack.
 Qualifications and Skills 
 Degree in Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace or Robotics Engineering, or a related field
 Working proficiency in C/C++ and Python: you can read, debug and patch existing code and write small tools and scripts
 Comfortable in Linux environments, including the command line, logs, Docker and basic networking (IP, TCP/UDP)
 Hands-on hardware-software integration: system bring-up, wiring and connectors, and embedded interfaces (UART, CAN, I2C, SPI) at a practical level
 Structured troubleshooting: you can isolate whether a problem is software, hardware, configuration or RF, often under time pressure in the field
 Strong communicator: you can explain technical issues clearly to customers and operators, and report findings back to engineering in a way they can act on
 Willing to travel and work on-site with customers, including at test ranges and in field environments
 EU citizenship (required for security clearance and customer requirements)
 Nice-to-have 
 Experience with PX4 or ArduPilot, MAVLink, QGroundControl or mission planning tools
 UAV flight testing and validation in operational environments
 Experience with datalinks and radio systems
 Previous customer-facing or field engineering role, especially with defense or government customers
 German language skills

About TACTILIA 
 At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI. Spun out of SCHUNK, the global market leader in gripping technology, we combine a decade of robotic-hand expertise and real industrial access with the speed and ambition of a deep-tech startup.
 This isn't a research project waiting for its first customer. We already have a product, customers are ready to use it, and we are launching now. Your work will directly shape the electronics, actuators, and embedded systems that make that possible.
 You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?
 The Role 
 You design the mechanics of our robotic hands — from the kinematics of a single finger to a complete hand ready for series production.
 Multiple drives, gear trains, tendons, tactile sensors and electronics have to fit into a human-sized envelope while surviving hundreds of thousands of cycles. Every millimetre matters, and almost every design decision affects another discipline.
 You work hands-on between CAD, test rig and workshop, and report to the CTO.
 What you will do: 
 CAD design. Design components, mechanisms and assemblies within tightly constrained envelopes, owning the design from concept through production release.
 Mechanism & kinematics. Design finger and thumb kinematics, tendon and spindle drives, joints and bearings. Calculate motion envelopes, trajectories, gripping forces and transmission ratios.
 Calculation & validation. Validate designs through structural and fatigue calculations, FEA, tolerance stack-ups and GD&T before parts are manufactured.
 Material selection. Select and qualify materials for lightweight structures, wear surfaces, tendons and elastomeric gripping surfaces, and characterise their behaviour under real loads and contact conditions.
 Assembly design. Design assemblies for efficient assembly, adjustment-free interfaces, serviceability and repair. Specify the required fixtures and tooling.
 Design for manufacturing. Design for the intended manufacturing process from the outset — machining, injection moulding, sheet metal, additive manufacturing — balancing cost, tolerances and production volumes.
 Prototyping & testing. Build prototypes, design test rigs and endurance setups, run cycle and load tests, and drive failures to root cause.
 Documentation & release. Create drawings and BOMs, manage design changes and configuration, and support product development reviews.
 Suppliers & production. Work with machine shops, material suppliers and manufacturing partners from first prototype through pilot series and production ramp-up.
 Cross-functional integration. Work closely with Electronics, Sensors and Software to align packaging, interfaces and load paths across the complete system.
 What you bring: 
 Degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, precision engineering, or a comparable qualification.
 5–10 years of experience in mechanical design of precision mechatronic products, including at least one product taken through to series production.
 Advanced 3D CAD skills in CATIA, NX, SolidWorks, Creo or comparable systems, with confident 2D drawing creation and GD&T.
 Strong understanding of mechanism design: linkages, gear trains, bearings, shafts, power transmission, backlash and stiffness.

About the role 
 Linkup is the web search engine built for AI. Our infrastructure crawls, indexes and serves the live web to AI agents, and it’s scaling fast.
 We’re looking for a top‑tier Machine Learning Engineer to join Linkup and work hand‑in‑hand with our CTO, Denis Charrier , and the rest of the tech team.
 Your core responsibilities will be to:
Design, train and ship ranking and retrieval models for AI agents
 Design, train and ship ranking and retrieval models for AI agents
 Bring new ranking signals into the engine, beyond pure relevance
 Build the evaluation framework that tells us what really improves search quality
 Optimize model serving for latency and GPU cost
 Turn customer and benchmark feedback into ranking improvements, with clear before/after numbers
   Requirements 
 You’re a great match if you:
 Are excited to help build Google for AI agents- and believe in Linkup’s mission 
 Have strong hands-on experience in information retrieval, ranking or search in production.
 Build rigorous evals and check the data behind every number
 Care about latency, cost and reliability as much as model quality
 Thrive in a fast-paced, high-ownership startup environment
   Example Projects 
 Ship a new ranking model to production and prove the gain on our eval sets
 Push our models to the next level: better answers, lower latency, lower cost per query
 Build and maintain the evaluations framework that measures every change to our search engine
   Our Stack 
 Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face, vLLM, Ray, Spark / Databricks, Vespa, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Terraform
 Details 
 The ideal candidate will play a central role in our engineering team, partnering closely with the founders. The models you ship will decide what thousands of AI products read every day.
 We offer a flexible remote‑work policy- see the details here .
 Join us and leverage your expertise to push the boundaries of AI!
   About Linkup 
   Our Vision 
 We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web . These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.
 AI agents need web search . To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.
 Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs . Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.
 Web 2.0 is sunsetting . The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google’s ad‑driven model has no natural home.
 Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up . We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.
 Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup. 
   Our Mission 
 Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.
 Our mission is to deliver the world’s freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.
   Our Culture 
 Our culture is built on the following values:
 Mission . We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.
 Speed . We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.
 Ownership . We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.
 Teamwork . Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.
 Humility . We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.
 We expect all team member to take an active role in shaping our company culture.
   Our Team 
 We are a small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents.
 A bit more about our 3 co-founders:
 Philippe Mizrahi- Led the development of Lyft’s Autonomous Vehicles marketplace. Previously launched Amundsen , an open source search engine.
 Denis Charrier - Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience.
 Boris Toledano - Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

 About The Job 
 As a Forward Software Engineer, you will build the systems behind some of the hardest problems Mistral takes on.
 You join our team of engineers in Applied AI. We gravitate towards hard problems, decide how to solve them, and ship fast. You work closely with our customer-facing teams, and what works goes into production with our customers and across the company. When a project needs it, you work directly on customer engagements.
 We're looking for a strong software engineer who has shipped agentic or GenAI systems to production. You've felt the pain of agents that work in the demo and fall apart on real tasks: tool calls that fail silently, loops that never end, and quality that drifts after launch. That production depth is your edge. You build across the stack, and you'd rather ship a plain UI on a solid foundation than a polished UI on a fragile one.
 You think like a founder. You start from the customer's problem, not the technology. You measure success by the value you deliver, and you care about building experiences people love to use. You like working at the edge of what AI can do today, and you push past it.

 Security is a big part of where we're heading. If you're drawn to it, that's a strong plus. Curiosity about how systems break, and a habit of learning fast from the people who know the domain, matter. Experience at a security company counts too.
 What you will do 
 Build AI systems end to end, from first prototype to production.
 Design the agent architecture: orchestration, tool use, memory, retrieval, and the interfaces between agents and the systems they act on.
 Build across the stack, from backend services and APIs to the interfaces people use to work with agents.
 Turn what works for one customer into patterns and platforms that work across many, without rebuilding each time.
 Make systems hold up under real load: throughput, latency, cost, and failure recovery are part of the design from the start.
 Build security into agents from day one: permissions, sandboxing, prompt-injection defenses, and audit trails for agents that touch sensitive systems.
 Build the evaluation loop: task-level evals, tracing, and checks that catch agent failures and quality drift before customers do.
 Work with researchers, engineers, and customer-facing teams to turn hard problems into systems people rely on.
 What We're Looking For 
 You have 5+ years building production software, with at least one agentic or GenAI system shipped to production that you ran after launch.
 You have full ability to ship across the stack: proficient NodeJS e.g. NextJS/Express/Fastify or similar or Python e.g. FastAPI. You are confident with TypeScript + React/NextJS or similar. Solid beats polished.
 You have hands-on depth in agent design: orchestration, tool use, retrieval, evaluation, and the ways agents fail in the real world.
 You work autonomously: you find the problem, decide the approach, and own the outcome.
 You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences, and are fluent in English.
 You ship in increments and are obsessed with time to value
 You have product judgment: you learn what users need through customer-facing teams, cut scope hard, and care how the result feels to use.
 Ideally you have 
 Open-source contributions, particularly in agents or LLMs.
 Experience deploying and running what you build: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and AWS, GCP, or Azure.
 A security background in application, cloud, or AI security, such as prompt injection, securing agents, or supply chain (SBOM, SLSA). If that's you, flag it in your application.
 Experience building for security workflows, such as alert triage, threat hunting, or investigation agents, or with SIEM, XDR, or SOAR tooling.
 How We Work in Applied AI

 What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

 The Role

items.jobTitle: CENTRALE LYON - Post Doctoral Open and Flexible System-Level Evaluation Framework for Emerging AI Computing Architectures
items.jobDescription:
Emerging computing technologies – non-volatile and ferroelectric memories, analog and digital in-memory computing, silicon photonics, 3D integration, and heterogeneous chiplets – offer major gains in energy efficiency, latency, bandwidth, and functionality. Their potential cannot, however, be established from device or circuit results alone: it requires a rigorous link between technology characteristics, architectural choices, workload mapping, and application-level figures of merit. 
 The Electronics group at the Lyon Institute of Nanotechnology (INL) is seeking a (m/f) postdoctoral researcher to develop an open, modular and extensible system-level evaluation framework for design space exploration (DSE) and system-design-technology co-optimization (SDTCO) of emerging computing architectures. The focus is at the interface of computer architecture, accelerator design, performance modelling and hardware-software codesign, while making systematic use of lower-level device, circuit and array results so that architectural conclusions remain physically credible. 
 The objective is to convert low-level results – compact models, measured or simulated KPIs, variability and reliability constraints, and multi-objective Pareto fronts – into parameterized architectural models supporting efficient exploration of accelerators for emerging AI workloads. The framework must enable both bottom-up projection, from device/circuit/array choices toward system performance, and top-down constraint propagation, from targets for energy, latency, throughput, accuracy, robustness and area toward technology and circuit requirements. It will consolidate ongoing INL activities in predictive system assessment, DTCO, emerging memories, compute-in-memory and photonic computing, integrating or extending existing components with emphasis on openness, reproducibility and reusability. 
 A core scientific challenge is to represent cross-layer trade-offs without hiding their origin: rather than isolated energy or latency numbers, the framework should expose bottlenecks, sensitivities, feasibility limits, break-even points and opportunities and identify the regimes in which a technology becomes advantageous. Target workloads span edge inference through to transformer-inspired models, with use cases in vision, audio and sensor processing, sparse and vector/matrix operations, and on-device learning. 
 Expected outcomes: a maintainable evaluation environment combining fast exploration with selected higherfidelity validation paths; cross-layer models and interface contracts, reusable data schemes, benchmarking flows, system-level Pareto analyses and design guidelines for emerging AI accelerators – a decision-support instrument for future research projects.
 Candidate profile: PhD in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related discipline, with a strong background in several of: computer architecture and AI accelerators; performance, energy and area modelling; design space exploration and multi-objective optimization; hardwaresoftware co-design and workload mapping; emerging memories, compute-in-memory or photonic computing. Strong Python skills and sound software-engineering practice are essential; experience with SystemC, C/C++, RISCV simulation, QEMU, PyTorch/ONNX workload flows, architecture simulators (NeuroSim, CiMLoop/AccelForge, Timeloop or similar) will be appreciated. Familiarity with circuit-level modelling or EDA is an asset, but the focus is architectural and system-level research. 
 Environment: the position is hosted by the Electronics group at INL (UMR CNRS 5270), Ecole Centrale de Lyon, Écully, France – an interdisciplinary environment spanning devices, circuits, architectures, design automation, photonics and integrated systems, with national and European collaborations. 
 Starting date: Fall 2026

Jij zorgt dat AI niet bij een financiële pilot blijft, maar helpt in het echte werk. 
 Een slimme AI-demo maakt indruk. Maar pas als analisten en medewerkers er elke dag mee werken, wordt technologie waardevol. Zeker in finance, waar betrouwbaarheid, controleerbaarheid en regelgeving nooit bijzaak zijn.
 Als Senior Forward Deployed AI Engineer ben je erbij vanaf het eerste gesprek. Je brengt "we willen iets met AI" binnen weken terug tot een use case die je kunt testen, of je zegt eerlijk dat het (nog) niet kan. Daarna ontwerp en bouw je de oplossing en breng je hem live in cycli van dagen. En dan maak je jezelf overbodig.
 Wat ga je doen? 
 Je slaat de brug tussen business en techniek: je zit aan tafel bij de klant, ontwerpt de oplossing en implementeert vaak ook zelf.
 Use cases scherp krijgen: samen met business development voer je discoverygesprekken, toets je use cases aan echte data en systemen en bouw je in dagen een proof-of-value.
 Ontwerpen en uitvoeren: je ontwerpt de agentic architectuur, kiest per situatie het patroon dat past en brengt de oplossing in korte cycli naar productie, samen met onze AI Engineers.
 Overdragen en meten: de klant kan de oplossing zelf draaien, en na go-live meet je of hij echt gebruikt wordt. Dát is je maatstaf.
 Ons slimmer maken: wat je leert, maak je herbruikbaar voor de volgende klant, en je helpt nieuwe FDE's op weg.
 Ongeveer 10% van je tijd gaat naar pre-sales en 90% naar delivery; business development is commercieel eigenaar.
 Van KYC tot complexe financiële processen 
 Je kent de werkelijkheid achter KYC/AML, klantacceptatie, klachten- en schadeafhandeling, financiële rapportage, risk en compliance. Denk aan:
 KYC-dossiers die agents voorbereiden met herleidbare bronnen, zodat analisten sneller onderbouwd beslissen.
 Documenten en signalen die samenkomen voor een klachten- of schadeteam.
 Rapportages die nu handwerk zijn, geautomatiseerd binnen de kaders van DORA en de EU AI Act.
 Wat breng je mee? 
 Aantoonbare ervaring in finance: je kent de processen, data, systemen en risico's van binnenuit.
 Je hebt AI-oplossingen met LLM's en agents ontworpen, in productie gebracht én onderhouden, inclusief evals, guardrails, monitoring en security.
 Sterk in Python en SQL, en hands-on met minimaal één cloud (Azure, AWS of GCP) en een dataplatform zoals Databricks, Snowflake of Fabric.
 Je werkt dagelijks met coding agents en beoordeelt kritisch wat ze opleveren.
 Ervaring in een klantgerichte rol, zoals consultancy, pre-sales, solutions engineering of je eigen startup.
 Je spreekt en schrijft vloeiend Nederlands en Engels.
Mooi meegenomen: ervaring met DORA, model risk management of audit trails, en met klassieke ML zoals fraude- en risicomodellen.
 Wat dit níet is 
 Geen individuele detachering. Je werkt aan projecten namens adesso, met een team achter je.
 Geen PoC-kerkhof. We bouwen om te gebruiken.
 Geen slides zonder code. Je advies komt met een werkende versie.
 Geen agent omdat het kan. Soms is de simpelste oplossing de beste, en dat zeg je dan.
 Het team 
 Je wordt onderdeel van ons AI Engineering-team: AI engineering consultants in twee rollen. De Forward Deployed AI Engineer (FDE) is eigenaar van het klantprobleem en ontwerpt de oplossing, inclusief de agentic architectuur. De AI Engineer gaat de diepte in op bouw, data, MLOps en schaal, en denkt vanaf de klantvraag mee over de juiste aanpak.
 Je krijgt ruimte om je eigen werk vorm te geven, maar je bent nooit alleen verantwoordelijk voor alle specialismen.
 Twijfel je welke rol het best bij je past? Solliciteer dan gewoon; we kijken samen. 
 Waarom adesso? Omdat je bij ons écht kunt meebouwen. 
 Bij adesso Nederland draait het om meer dan alleen technologie. We bouwen slimme oplossingen die daadwerkelijk waarde toevoegen voor onze klanten. Geen eindeloze experimenten of AI omdat het hip is, maar technologie die werkt en impact maakt.
 We zijn onderdeel van de internationale adesso Group, met ruim 11.500 collega's op meer dan 60 locaties. Tegelijkertijd zijn we in Nederland een relatief klein en persoonlijk team, met korte lijnen, veel vrijheid en ruimte voor eigen initiatief.
 Groot genoeg om impact te maken, klein genoeg om het verschil te voelen.
 AI-native: wij omarmen AI, ook in ons eigen werk 
 We geloven dat AI fundamenteel verandert hoe we software bouwen, met data werken en klanten helpen. Daarom bouwen we niet aan losse experimenten, maar aan dataplatformen, AI-first applicaties en agentic oplossingen die echt onderdeel worden van bedrijfsprocessen.
 Dat geldt ook voor hoe we zelf werken. Met onze Agentic Delivery-aanpak en eigen tools kun je echt vliegen:
 Context en kennisbank: agents werken met wat er écht speelt bij de klant, en kennis en beslissingen blijven herleidbaar voor mens én agent.
 AgentOps en governance: zicht op wat agents doen en controle over wat ze mogen, zodat ze veilig en binnen de regels werken.
 adSCAILE: ons eigen framework waarmee je samen met AI-agents bouwt, geïntegreerd, veilig en traceerbaar, in cycli van twee tot vier dagen in plaats van sprints van weken.
 Je gebruikt deze tools dagelijks en helpt ze verder te ontwikkelen. adesso is bovendien Select Partner in het Claude Partner Network van Anthropic. En we blijven kritisch: niet alles hoeft met AI. De beste oplossing staat altijd voorop.
 En misschien wel het belangrijkste: de mensen 
 Je komt terecht in een team waar vakmanschap, ondernemerschap en kennisdeling centraal staan. Je werkt met ervaren specialisten en groeit door in technische visie en in verantwoordelijkheid voor klantrelaties.
 We houden van collega's die nieuwsgierig zijn, kennis delen en elkaar verder helpen. Mensen die goed zijn in hun vak, maar ook plezier hebben in samenwerken. Je krijgt bij ons vertrouwen, verantwoordelijkheid en de vrijheid om ideeën daadwerkelijk uit te voeren.
 Wat krijg je van ons? 
 €5.850–€7.150 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur;
 8% vakantiegeld;
 Contract voor 32 tot 40 uur per week;
 Een leaseauto of mobiliteitsvergoeding naar keuze, bovenop je salaris;
 27 vakantiedagen en 4 studiedagen;
 €3.600 persoonlijk ontwikkelbudget per jaar en ruimte voor certificeringen;
 Hybride werken met flexibele werktijden;
 Goede pensioenregeling;
 Doorgroeimogelijkheden in een specialistenspoor;
 Internationale kennis en ontwikkelmogelijkheden, gecombineerd met een hecht Nederlands team;
 Zullen we kennismaken? 
 Je hoeft niet aan ieder technisch punt te voldoen. We zijn vooral benieuwd naar wat je hebt gebouwd, welke keuzes je hebt gemaakt en waar je naartoe wilt groeien.
 Een cv of LinkedIn-profiel is genoeg om het gesprek te starten. Daarna volgen een kennismaking, een technisch gesprek en een praktijkcase.
 Bij adesso werk je niet alleen aan de technologie van morgen. Je krijgt ook de ruimte om mee te bepalen hoe we die bouwen.

items.jobDescription:
The rules of building are being rewritten. Come write them with us. 
 Every few decades, the way companies are built gets reinvented from scratch. That is happening right now, and the people who learn to build in this new world first will define the next twenty years. Superstars are being made this year, not in ten. 
 HelloPrint is a €100M+ e-commerce company serving businesses across Europe and the US. We are rebuilding the entire company as AI-first: our platform, customer service, operations, and how we design, price, sell, and deliver. Every piece of technology we run is being rewritten as we speak. 
We are doing it with a small, senior, very fast AI development team working shoulder to shoulder with our business leads. Now we are opening a handful of seats for young builders who want to grow faster than any graduate scheme, bootcamp, or big-tech ladder could ever let them. 
 We don't care if you are 16, 25 or 30, whether you are self-taught, hacking in high school, or finishing a degree at TU Delft or TU/e—we care about what you have built and how fast you solve hard problems. 
The HelloPrint AI Residency is how you start. It is a permanent role from day one: your first year is a structured residency where you rotate across our most important AI projects, build alongside the team and learn at full speed. After that, you keep growing - in the direction where you have the most impact. 
 What you will actually do: 
 You will not get a training plan, a sandbox project or six months of shadowing. From week one, you build real things that real customers and colleagues use, on the projects that matter most to the company. You sit next to the founders, next to the engineers who are rebuilding our platform, and next to the business leads who own the outcomes. You get a lot of freedom and real responsibility, plus honest, direct guidance and feedback from people who have built this before.
 The kind of work you could be on in your first months: 
 Agentic Commerce : making HelloPrint discoverable and orderable through AI assistants, so a customer can order business cards from inside a chat. 
 AI Design Studio : letting customers create a print-ready design from a single sentence. 
 AI-first customer service : replacing classic ticketing with agents that resolve questions, check artwork and handle orders end to end. 
 Internal agent swarms : automating finance, purchasing, pricing and operations work that today still takes people hours. 
 Whatever you spot next : if you see something we should build, you pitch it, and if it is good, you build it. 
 We work with almost every modern framework and model, and we change our tools the moment something better appears. You will ship, measure, throw away and ship again - every week. 
 Who you are: 
 You are a builder before anything else . You have shipped things nobody asked you to build: an app, an agent, a bot, a tool your friends actually use, a side business, an open-source contribution, a weird experiment that taught you something. You probably have more GitHub commits, demos or deployed projects than most people twice your age. 
 You are extremely curious and extremely critical. You read the new model release the day it drops and try it that evening. You question every assumption, including ours, and you can explain why. You are never satisfied with "it works" — you want to know why it works, and how it could be ten times better. 
 You want to get better every single day, and you treat feedback as fuel rather than criticism. You take ownership: when something breaks, you fix it; when something is unclear, you go and find out. 
 You have a solid grasp of backend and software fundamentals (Python, APIs, databases) or the raw learning capacity to pick them up in weeks.
 You will probably recognise yourself in most of this: 
 You build with AI every day: Claude, Cursor, Lovable, agents, APIs, whatever gets you there fastest. 
 You can show us concrete proof of work, not just tell us about it. 
 You move fast without being sloppy, and you care about the details the customer sees. 
 You are comfortable not knowing the answer, and you find it quickly. 
 You communicate clearly in English, in writing and out loud.
What we do not require: a degree, a minimum age, years of experience or a perfect CV. If you are still in school or university, we will make it work around that. 
 What you get: 
 The honest pitch: you will learn more here in one year than in five years almost anywhere else , because you will be building real systems for a real company that is reinventing itself, with the people who are leading that change. 
A contract from day one. The Residency is your first year at HelloPrint, not a trial period or an internship. 
 Direct access to the founders and to a senior AI development team who review your work and push you. 
 Ownership from day one : your name on projects that change how a €100M+ company runs. 
 The best tools, no budget debates : the newest models, coding agents and frameworks, as soon as they are worth using. 
 A growth path that follows your output, not your age : if you outgrow your role in six months, your role grows with you. 
 A fast, flat, no-politics team in Rotterdam, with a hands-on culture and a high bar. 
 Flexible set-up : full-time, or part-time alongside your studies. We care about what you deliver.
 Salary and contract are tailored to your situation and your level, and we pay properly for real talent.
 How to apply: 
 Skip the cover letter. Show us what you have built.
 Send us three things: 
 Your best project : a link to something you built: a live product, a repo, a demo video. Tell us in a few sentences what it does and what you would do differently now. 
 Something you think is broken : one thing about HelloPrint (our website, our ordering flow, anything) that you would rebuild with AI, and how you would do it. 
 A short intro : who you are and what you are obsessed with right now. Five sentences is plenty.
 What happens next: 
 We read every application ourselves and reply within 5 days if you’re up to the next round 
 A 15-minute call with one of our builders or founders about your projects. 
 A Builders Day in our office: Together with other builders, you meet the team and if we have a click, you work on an assignment 
 A conversation with the founders, and a decision the same day.
 We would rather hear from you too early than too late. If you are not sure you are ready, apply anyway;  your work will answer that question for us. At HelloPrint, we believe diversity makes us better. We're building a workplace where everyone can be themselves, grow, and do their best work regardless of background, identity, or perspective. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

About Telnyx 
 Telnyx is an industry leader that's not just imagining the future of global connectivity—we're building it. From architecting and amplifying the reach of a private, global, multi-cloud IP network , to bringing hyperlocal edge technology right to your fingertips through intuitive APIs, we're shaping a new era of seamless interconnection between people, devices, and applications. 
 We're driven by a desire to transform and modernize what's antiquated, automate the manual, and solve real-world problems through innovative connectivity solutions. As a testament to our success, we're proud to stand as a financially stable and profitable company. Our robust profitability allows us not only to invest in pioneering technologies but also to foster an environment of continuous learning and growth for our team. 
 Our collective vision is a world where borderless connectivity fuels limitless innovation. By joining us, you can be part of laying the foundations for this interconnected future. We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers. 
 The Role 
We're building a local Enterprise Sales Pod in Munich — one AE and one Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), working together to build a Telnyx enterprise business in your market. You'll embed directly with enterprise customers to architect and ship production systems on Telnyx's global network — voice, messaging, AI, and wireless.
This isn't about demoing products. It's about building real solutions that work at scale.
You'll work side-by-side with a dedicated Enterprise AE — not a demo resource, but a commercial partner who owns the named-account list, builds executive relationships, and closes the deal. You own the technical side: discovery, architecture, POC, and production go-live. You win together. No throw-over-the-wall.
 The Pod Model 
 Enterprise AE — owns the named-account list, builds executive relationships, gets in the room, owns commercial qualification and close, expands the account. .
 Forward Deployed Engineer — owns technical discovery, designs the architecture, builds the POC when gated, gets the first workload live, removes blockers and finds the next workload.
We sell the workload, not the SKU. Customers buy a production outcome — an AI contact center, a SOC/NOC agent, global communications, connected mobility, or enterprise inference — that runs on Telnyx primitives (voice, messaging, numbers, wireless, Voice AI, inference, agents, connectivity). You lead with the outcome conversation, not a product menu.
 What You'll Do 
• Embed with enterprise customers to understand their communications workflows, AI use cases, and integration challenges firsthand
• Build and deploy custom implementations: AI Voice Assistants, Telnyx APIs (Voice, Messaging, Fax, Wireless), WebRTC
• Run open-weight LLMs in customer environments — consume GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen, and MiniMax through Telnyx Inference (OpenAI-compatible API; there's no model infrastructure for you to run), or deploy self-hosted stacks (Llama, Mistral, and region-specific models like Aleph Alpha's Luminous, or sovereign EU models) behind your own serving engine when air-gapped or sovereign-cloud requirements demand it
• Deploy and operate LiteLLM as the model gateway in customer environments: a unified OpenAI-compatible interface across self-hosted open-weight models and hosted providers, with routing, load balancing, retries and fallbacks, rate limits, and per-team virtual keys
• Instrument and govern LLM usage through the gateway — cost tracking and budgets, caching, logging and observability (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, or similar), and guardrails — so customers can see and control what their AI workloads are doing
• Wire production observability for everything you ship — metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and alerting (e.g. Prometheus + Grafana for metrics, OpenTelemetry for traces, Graylog or ELK for logs — or the customer's existing stack) — so you and the customer's ops team both know what "healthy" looks like and what pages whom when it isn't
• Design model routing strategies for real-time voice workloads, balancing latency, cost, and quality, with sane fallback behavior when a provider degrades
• Make the build-vs-buy case between self-hosted open-weight models and hosted frontier APIs, and keep the customer's application code portable across both
• Adapt models to customer domains: prompt and RAG pipelines and evaluation harnesses for German-language use cases and DACH-specific regulatory environments (GDPR, EU AI Act, German data localization)
• Lead POCs, pilots, and production launches from whiteboard to go-live
• Own customer outcomes — stay engaged until the solution is live and stable
• Collaborate directly with Product and Engineering to shape the roadmap based on field insights from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
• Create clear technical documentation, runbooks, and maintainable solutions for handoff 
 • Troubleshoot and resolve complex integration issues alongside customer teams
 What We're Looking For 
• CS degree or equivalent experience
• 3+ years building and shipping production software — you've written code that real users depended on, you've been on-call for it, and you've debugged it when things broke. (A consulting background counts if this is also true of you.)
• Proficiency in multiple languages: Python, Node.js/TypeScript, Go — you're more dangerous in some than others. (Telnyx Edge Compute — functions and stateful actors — is TypeScript, so that one pulls double duty.)
• Practical understanding of what breaks in front of a model in production: provider rate limits and quotas, timeout and retry behavior, streaming, token accounting and cost attribution, and the failure modes that only show up under concurrency
• Comfortable deploying containerized services on Kubernetes, with secrets management, config, and upgrades as part of the deployment story
• You've wired observability and been paged because of it — Prometheus + Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Graylog, ELK, or equivalent. You know what to monitor, what to alert on, and what "healthy" looks like
• High-concurrency experience — Kafka, message queues, or event streams at real scale. When throughput spikes you know what breaks — consumer lag, backpressure, hot partitions, rebalance stalls — and what absorbs it: partitioning, consumer groups, parallelism up to your partition count
• You've built APIs from scratch, not just consumed them — OpenAPI spec, REST/GraphQL design, auth, rate limiting, versioning, idempotency
• Event-driven thinking and cloud-native instincts
• Exposure to SIP, WebRTC, or real-time voice/messaging systems
• Self-sufficient by default — there's no engineering team behind you. You read the code and the docs, ask the customer (not your manager), and make sound engineering judgment calls on your own
• Customer-facing engineering experience — you can run discovery with a customer's engineers and present to their executives in the same week
• Ability to translate "it's not working" into root cause
• Comfortable working on customer sites and in high-stakes technical conversations
• Excellent written and verbal communication in English and German. You can run whiteboard sessions, live troubleshooting, and escalations with customer engineering teams.
• Based in Munich, or willing to relocate — this is a hybrid role with travel across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
• Legally authorized to work in Germany, or eligible for sponsorship
 Bonus Points For 
• Experience with AI voice assistants, STT/TTS, or LLM-based conversational systems
• Building eval sets for a specific domain
• Hands-on production experience with an LLM gateway — LiteLLM, Portkey, Kong AI Gateway, or an in-house OpenAI-compatible proxy — including config-driven model definitions, routing and fallback rules, and virtual key management
• Familiarity with the open-weight model landscape and the trade-offs between regional and multilingual models, including EU sovereign AI initiatives (Gaia-X, Aleph Alpha, European LLM projects)
• Experience with an inference serving engine behind the gateway — vLLM, SGLang, or TGI for production serving; Ollama for lightweight on-prem — and sizing GPU capacity for self-hosted models (KV-cache footprint, concurrent batch size, and context length against VRAM)
• SQL proficiency (Postgres, MySQL, Oracle)
• ETL and data wrangling experience
• CI/CD pipeline design and automation
• Background in telecom, CPaaS, or high-growth SaaS
• Experience with sovereign or on-prem cloud deployments and DACH regulatory frameworks (GDPR, EU AI Act, German data sovereignty and localization requirements, Swiss data protection)
• Security mindset (IAM, encryption, audit logging)

items.jobDescription:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments. 
 We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions. 
 WHY JOIN US 
 The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty. 
 You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms. 
 We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing. 
 ABOUT THE TEAM 
 The Data Operations team owns the entire data lifecycle behind STARK's AI stack: collection, acquisition, generation, curation, and management. We run our own data-collection campaigns across Europe, evaluate new sensors and platforms, and build the internal data platform that turns raw recordings into ready-to-use datasets. Everything we produce feeds directly into the perception and autonomy systems deployed on STARK's platforms — a real data advantage is built, not bought. The team is scaling up right now: real scope, direct impact, no legacy.
 YOUR MISSION 
 You own our data-collection flights. When the perception team needs a specific dataset — a new camera at a new angle, a lidar over specific terrain, a thermal sensor at dusk — you plan the campaign, configure and tune the platform, fly the mission, and bring clean data home. Our hardware engineer builds the rigs and mounts, our robotics engineer makes the sensors record — you make it all fly, reliably, again and again. This is a role for someone with real stick time and real PX4/ArduPilot depth: not a desk job with occasional field trips, but the other way around.
 WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK 
 Plan and execute field data-collection campaigns across Europe: flight planning, site assessment, pre-flight checks, piloting, logging, and post-flight data offload
 Configure, tune, and troubleshoot PX4/ArduPilot flight stacks for stable, repeatable data-collection flights
 Analyze flight logs to diagnose issues and continuously improve platform reliability
 Operate sensor payloads (cameras, gimbals, lidar, GNSS/IMU) during missions and verify recordings on-site
 Keep the fleet mission-ready: maintenance, repairs, spare parts, battery management, and configuration control
 Work with our hardware and robotics engineers on payload integration — you define what the platform needs to fly well
 Maintain flight logs and campaign documentation so every flight produces usable, traceable data
 Ensure operations comply with aviation regulations (EU drone rules) and internal safety procedures
 WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION 
 Confident, experienced drone pilot with substantial real-world flight hours (multirotor; fixed-wing a plus), holding an EU A2/A3 certificate or willing to obtain quickly
 Solid practical knowledge of PX4 and/or ArduPilot: configuration, parameter tuning, log analysis, MAVLink basics
 Hands-on experience assembling, repairing, and maintaining drones — comfortable with soldering, wiring, and multimeter debugging
 Experience operating sensor payloads and ground control stations in the field
 Practical, structured, and safety-conscious — you find the loose cable before it becomes a crash
 Willingness to travel regularly for field campaigns and work outdoors in various conditions
 Good communication skills in English (German is a plus)
 NICE TO HAVE 
 Scripting skills (Python, Bash) for flight log processing and data offload automation
 CAD basics (Fusion 360, SolidWorks) and 3D-printing experience
 Experience with ROS/ROS2 recording setups or companion computers (Jetson, Raspberry Pi)
 Background in FPV, drone racing, RC modeling, competition teams, or maker culture
 Experience with camera settings and image quality trade-offs for data collection
 German driving license class B (field campaigns)

 Due to the nature of our work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate security clearance required for this position. Details will be provided during the recruitment process.

CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at  www.coreweave.com . 
 We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer. 
 About the Team 
 Launchables is CoreWeave's platform for building Physical Intelligence. We bring simulation, training and evaluation tools into a common platform, allowing robotics, autonomous systems and engineering teams to focus on their applications while Launchables handles common execution and infrastructure needs.
 We turn specialist Physical AI software into capabilities that researchers and engineers can use, adapt and build upon. Our work combines strong software engineering with applied domain knowledge to make complex workloads accessible, reproducible and useful in real-world environments.
 As a Staff Software Engineer, Workloads - Physical AI, you will develop engine integrations, application code, adapters, templates and developer tools that make specialist software available through Launchables. You will work directly with researchers and engineers to understand their tasks, assumptions, dependencies and expected outcomes, translating these into interfaces and configurations that preserve the capabilities they need.
 You will take ownership of how users configure, run, customise and evaluate workloads. This includes defining meaningful inputs, defaults, constraints and outputs; building command-line and API interfaces; and creating examples and documentation that help users extend existing templates or author their own. You will establish appropriate validation for packaging, execution and application outcomes, working with domain specialists to make evaluation criteria and their limitations clear.
 You will profile workloads to improve preparation time, GPU utilisation, concurrency and data movement while preserving the intended computation. You will also capture the inputs, versions, settings and execution conditions needed to reproduce runs, with logs, metrics and artefacts that help users diagnose failures, compare experiments and interpret results.
 Working alongside engineers responsible for the shared runtime and platform services, you will turn feedback from early users into better interfaces, defaults, tests and guidance. You will identify reusable patterns across integrations, shape shared platform capabilities, review designs and mentor colleagues. You will use coding agents and automation to accelerate development, applying the review, testing and domain judgement needed to ensure the resulting software behaves as intended.
 Qualifications: 
 Strong software engineering skills, demonstrated through dependable software or developer tools used by other people.
 Applied depth in at least one relevant area, such as robotics simulation, autonomous-vehicle evaluation, reinforcement learning, synthetic-data generation or engineering simulation.
 Experience making specialist or research software usable beyond its original author, including configuration, testing, documentation and diagnosis.
 Sound judgement about experimental assumptions, evaluation criteria, reproducibility and the conclusions a result supports.
 Familiarity with containerised execution and experience tracing problems across application and infrastructure boundaries.
 Comfortable learning unfamiliar tools and domains, working closely with specialists and recognising when their expertise is needed.
 Evidence of improving shared tools or engineering practices across multiple projects, with clear reasoning about what should be common and what should remain application-specific.
 Preferred Skills: 
 Experience developing software in Python, Go or C++.
 Familiarity with simulation and machine-learning frameworks.
 Experience profiling GPU workloads and identifying performance or resource bottlenecks.
 Experience with Kubernetes or workflow orchestration.
 Wondering if you're a good fit? 
 We believe in investing in our people, and value candidates who can bring their own diversified experiences to our teams - even if you aren't a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we've found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we'd love to talk.
 You enjoy turning specialist Physical AI software into dependable tools that other researchers and engineers can use independently.
 You care about making experiments understandable and reproducible, with clear evidence of what their results do and do not establish.
 You combine hands-on engineering with curiosity about unfamiliar domains, and enjoy helping colleagues build reusable, high-quality systems.
 We welcome relevant experience from industry, research engineering and academia. We are interested in what you have built, how others use it and the judgement you brought to making it work.
 Why CoreWeave? 
 At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We're in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We're not afraid of a little chaos, and we're constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:
 Be Curious at Your Core
 Act Like an Owner
 Empower Employees
 Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences
 Achieve More Together
 We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and enables the development of innovative solutions to complex problems. Come join us!

 The Role: 
 We're looking for an experienced, AI-native Systems Reliability Engineer to join our Engineering Team. This team works alongside our core development teams to support existing operations, with a mandate for continuous improvement and the goal to create systems that are as "hands-off" as possible. You'll work with our delivery teams throughout the development lifecycle to ensure systems delivered are scalable, robust, and supportable. You'll also work on optimising our software and infrastructure to improve reliability and decrease cost.
 You are agentic-first. You reach for AI to diagnose, script, automate and document as a matter of course, and you are at home operating within an AI-assisted delivery pipeline.
 There is an element of working on support issues arising in real time while also participating in DevOps tasks to implement changes and investigate problems.
 In both instances, the expectation is that AI does the first pass and you direct and verify it.
 Propellerhead operates a hybrid working model (work from our office and from your own home). While you must be based in Auckland for this role, we warmly welcome applications from across New Zealand and internationally who are planning to relocate to Auckland. This particular role requires regular in-person office attendance.
 We offer a culture built on trust, continuous learning, and meaningful impact. You'll join a team that values integrity over ego, and clarity over complexity.
 Role Responsibilities: 
 Working alongside core development teams to design cloud deployment architectures on Azure.
 Leading the provisioning of deployment environments - including all aspects of servers, services and networking - and communications with technical client stakeholders.
 Ensuring aspects of security, scalability, supportability and performance are implemented in solution architectures.
 Assisting development teams to build continuous integration and deployment pipelines using toolsets selected for the particular technology stack.
 Carrying out scheduled software releases in partnership with development teams where full automation has not yet been achieved.
 Configuring monitoring and alerting tools, and integrate into support desk software.
 Providing technical assistance to support ticket triaging and troubleshooting, while verifying the symptoms, impact and responsibility for further investigation.
 Actively participating in the diagnosis and remedy of reactive support issues during business hours and on a shared on-call after hours basis.
 Completing incident reports, including recommendations for ongoing mitigation. Implement mitigations in partnership with core development teams.
 Monitoring incident progress, and communicating status updates to clients.
 Designing and implementing proactive continuous improvement programmes for our solutions to minimise the occurrence of support issues.
 Automating first. When a task recurs, you build the automation rather than repeat it.
 Documenting, with AI-assistance, system architecture and configuration/ deployment processes; proactively sharing technical knowledge with support developers across multiple teams.
 Skills & Experience Required: 
 Previous experience as a Site/Systems Reliability Engineer, DevOps Engineer or equivalent role.
 Agentic-first: you are very comfortable using AI to diagnose, script, automate and document, and to work within an AI-assisted delivery pipeline. This is central to the role.
 Expertise developing scalable web applications.
 Some proficiency in Rust, Java, .NET or Go. Experience in JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Node.js, ReactJS, AngularJS or similar front-end frameworks.
 Proven scripting experience using PowerShell, Ruby, Python, shell or other common scripting languages, including the use of AI tools to help construct these.
 Strong experience in Microsoft Azure deployment architectures, Microsoft DevOps deployment pipelines, GitHub Actions, and Terraform.
 System administration of Linux cloud-based server environments.
 Troubleshooting and configuration of virtual networks.
 Familiarity with configuration of New Relic, Dynatrace or similar monitoring framework, including building dashboards and alerting integration.
 Some experience with AWS and Bamboo/Bitbucket Pipelines tools would be an advantage.
 Ability to easily switch context across different technologies and complex environments.
 Ability to remain calm under the pressure of high-priority issue resolution scenarios.
 Good judgement about when to trust an AI-generated diagnosis and when to verify by hand.
 A strong desire to learn and up-skill.
 You must be Auckland based for this role. We offer a hybrid working model (working from home and working on-site), however office attendance is currently required three days per week on our dedicated teams in-office days, and occasionally as needed due to client and team requirements.
 About Propellerhead: 
 Propellerhead is a leading software services company that designs, delivers, and maintains large-scale, custom-built digital platforms across a range of technologies. We place emphasis on producing technology which is meaningful, has value, and can make a difference in the world. We foster long lasting and trusting relationships with all our clients. Over our 20+ years in the market we have worked with a diverse range of commercial, non-profit, and government organisations.
 How We Build Software: 
 We build software by structuring solutions in a product-centric manner and focusing on continuously delivering measurable outcomes into production. Our work starts from real stakeholder needs and the value they unlock, with an AI-assisted pipeline now generating much of the code.As a result, our digital platforms are a mixture of custom components and external services which produce a powerful and engaging experience when combined.
 Benefits: 
 Be part of an innovative team, with a culture of learning and collaboration.
 Contribute to interesting, diverse, and commercially minded work for well-respected clients.
 Opportunity for professional growth and development.
 Fortnightly knowledge sharing sessions, with lunch.
 Competitive salary. Employee Share Purchase Scheme offering.
 This role is Auckland based, regular in-office attendance is required.  Work within our beautifully designed office and from home (hybrid working model).
 Propellerhead is an equal opportunity workplace which is free from discrimination.
 Cover Letter: 
 *Please note - only applications with a cover letter will be reviewed. 
 It's very important to us that you include a cover letter with your application - it's your chance to tell us more about who you are and what you value.
 At Propellerhead, we use AI thoughtfully as part of our delivery practices - considered integration helps us stay at the forefront of technology and create innovative, valuable solutions for our clients. 
 In recruitment, however, AI isn’t used to assess skills, experience or suitability for a role. Every application is reviewed by a real person to ensure a fair, engaged and thoughtfully human process. 
 Therefore we kindly ask that you refrain from using it in your application. We're excited to learn about your unique experiences and ideas, so please apply as your authentic self! 
 More: 
 Candidates that progress may be asked to agree to a police background check, credit history check, other assessments and provide evidence of qualifications.

 Compensation: 55-75k + 0.05% BSPCE (stock options)
 Our Team: 21 Engineers, 4 Technical Leads, 4 Squads
   About Escape 
 Escape is offensive security for the teams that are 100x outnumbered. We build AI agents that find and exploit vulnerabilities in modern applications, APIs, and microservices: the way a real attacker would, but at the speed of a CI pipeline.
 We're a Y Combinator W23 company. We just closed an $18M Series A in March 2026 led by Balderton Capital (with Uncorrelated Ventures, IRIS, and YC following on). Our customers and partners include Zoom, Schibsted, Wiz, Pandadoc, and a growing list of teams who've stopped pretending annual pen tests are enough. We're 40 people split between Paris and NYC, scaling to 80 in the next 12 months.
 The product surface is real: ASM, business-logic-aware DAST, and AI Pentesting GA-ing this year. The competitive thesis is that LLMs collapsed the cost of offensive engineering by 1000x, and the companies that ship that capability into production first will own the next decade of the category. We're betting we're those companies.

 Your work will help shape the core of Escape’s products. As a Junior Full-Stack Engineer, you’ll work closely with senior engineers and technical leads to deliver features and improvements across the product. This is a great learning opportunity for someone early in their engineering career who wants to dive into AI-powered cybersecurity, work across the stack, and see the impact of their work in production.

 1-2 years’ experience building web applications

 Motivation to learn TypeScript and modern frameworks like Svelte
 Familiarity with APIs (REST or GraphQL) and databases like PostgreSQL
 Interest in the intersection of AI, security, and high-impact products
 Strong communication and teamwork skills ready to ask questions and grow
   Nice to have: 
 Some exposure to security or DevSecOps concepts
 Experience at a startup or on small teams
     Ready to take your development skills to the next level and learn from passionate engineers? Apply now to join Escape and shape the future of AI-powered security!

items.jobTitle: Quantum Dot Process & Characterisation Engineer- Post-Growth Processing (Master)
items.jobDescription:
Quandela stands as a global leader in quantum computing, driven by groundbreaking technology and a strategic vision for scaling quantum solutions. The company’s unique ability to offer both hardware and software solutions, along with its commitment to build energy efficient datacenters and scalability, positions it to play a key role in the next wave of innovation, and in many strategic and sovereign industrial sectors. 
 Join Us at the Forefront of Quantum Computing Innovation 🚀
 Role overview 
 We are looking for a Process & Characterisation Engineer to prepare and validate GaAs/AlGaAs samples containing InAs quantum dots (QDs) through the first steps of our single-photon source fabrication flow.
 The role combines hands-on cleanroom processing – chemical treatment, PECVD deposition and high-temperature annealing – with optical characterisation of the QDs before and after each step. The data you produce decides whether a sample is ready to move forward, and how the process recipes should be adjusted.
 You will start by running an established, well-documented procedure with rigour and consistency. As you build expertise, the role is designed to grow: within your first year, you will contribute to optimising the process, automating the measurement setups and taking ownership of sample validation for these steps, working closely with both the Production and R&D teams.
 Sample preparation & processing (from day one) 
 Run the established step-by-step procedure for preparing GaAs/AlGaAs samples with InAs quantum dots.
 Carry out the cleanroom fabrication steps: chemical surface treatment, PECVD deposition and high-temperature annealing.
 Follow recipes and operating procedures precisely, and flag any deviation, drift or anomaly as soon as it appears.
 Contribute to a safe, disciplined and efficient cleanroom environment.
 Optical characterisation & validation 
 Measure QD optical properties before and after processing, using photoluminescence and white-field imaging, including at cryogenic temperature.
 Compare pre- and post-processing results against acceptance criteria to decide whether each sample can be released to the next fabrication steps.
 Adjust process recipes based on measurement results, within defined process windows.
 Data, reporting & traceability 
 Analyse measurement data using Python and report results clearly and regularly to the Production and R&D teams.
 Maintain the sample database so that every sample’s processing history and measurements are fully traceable.
 Keep process documentation and procedures up to date.
 Growing your scope (within the first year) 
 Contribute to the automation and optimisation of the optical measurement setups and data-acquisition pipeline.
 Propose, design and test improvements to the fabrication steps, using experimental data and the scientific literature.
 Take ownership of sample validation for these steps, including defining checks and acceptance criteria.
 Contribute to the development and qualification of new or additional process steps, together with the R&D team.
 Requirements 
 Required qualifications & experience 
 Master’s degree (Bac+5) in Materials Science, Semiconductor Physics, Optics, Micro/Nanofabrication or a related field.
 Solid foundations in semiconductor physics, particularly III-V materials.
 Solid foundations in optics and in semiconductor fabrication processes.
 Fluency in Python for data analysis.
 Excellent attention to detail and a rigorous approach to experimental work.
 Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
 Ability to investigate technical problems using experimental data and scientific literature.
 Clear documentation and communication skills.
 Fluent English, both written and spoken.
 Preferred qualifications 
 Hands-on cleanroom experience, ideally in III-V device fabrication: wet and dry etching, PECVD deposition, thermal processing.
 Hands-on experience with optical characterisation, including building and aligning optical setups (photoluminescence, white-field imaging).
 Experience with cryogenic measurements (e.g. 40 K Stirling cryostat).
 Experience automating instruments or measurement setups with Python.
 You enjoy hands-on work in the cleanroom and the lab every day, and you get satisfaction from a measurement done right and a sample that is fully traceable. You are comfortable applying an established procedure with rigour, and curious enough to ask why a result looks the way it does.
 Over time, you want to do more than follow the recipe: you are ready to propose ideas, make decisions based on experimental results and modify the process accordingly. You are autonomous, proactive, and enjoy working at the interface between Production and R&D.
 If you are passionate about semiconductor fabrication and quantum technologies, we would love to hear from you, even if you don’t tick every box.
 Benefits 
 Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience 
 Profit-sharing & company savings plan
 100% health coverage (Alan)
 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
 Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
 Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)
 What we offer: 
 A meaningful role with real ownership, from day one
 A team eager to collaborate and grow with you
 Daily exposure to the entire quantum stack — from high-level APIs to low-level firmware, and everything in between.
 Process 
 Talent Acquisition interview (30–45 minutes).
 Hiring Manager interview (45 minutes).
 Technical interview and team meeting.
 Two reference checks.
 Offer.
 (This process is provided for guidance only and may evolve depending on the roles) 
 At Quandela, we believe that the strength of our team is the plurality of experiences, perspectives, and journeys. We are committed to building a respectful, inclusive, and welcoming work environment. All applications are welcome.
